links.reason: The shared tribute formula is real: யானையொடு அரும்கலம் துறுத்துப் பணிந்துவழி மொழிதல் (fr. 1-2) against நன்கலம் களிற்றொடு ... வணங்கினர் வழிமொழிந்து (Aka 124.1-2), and Aka 124 does make the enemy's submission the condition of the man's return (இன்றே புகுதல் வாய்வது). But the akam poem does not extend or fulfil the praise fragment; the two simply use one formula in two genres, which is a same_image pairing rather than development.
links.text_issue: Fragment line 7 carries a repaired TSCII reading and the marker flagged the fragment's sense as uncertain.

links.reason: Neelakesi 776 attacks a causal thesis, that the effect pre-exists in its cause (வித்தினுள் உண்டென வேண்டுதி நீள்பனை), with a reductio about the hand holding the seed. Sivavakkiyar's ஆலவித்தில் ஆல்ஒடுங்கி is a simile for Parabrahman found within the self, not a claim about material causation. The tension rests on treating a mystic's image as the Sankhya doctrine, so the gains clause that the Siddhar 'meets an objection it never answers' stretches the image into a thesis.

295 asks whether the room of souls and pudgala (மன்னுயிர்க்கும் புற்கலக்கும் இடன்) would spill past the bound of all worlds if the two (dharma and adharma) did not exist. 759 states that space is one and runs through உலகு and அலோகம். Taken together they give the Jain reason why the world's limit cannot come from space, which neither verse states alone.

Aputhiran sets a condition as he releases the bowl into Gomukhi: ஓர் யாண்டு ஒரு நாள் தோன்று ... அருள் அறம் பூண்டு ஆங்கு ஆர் உயிர் ஓம்புநர் உளர்எனில் அவர் கைப் புகுவாய் (14:92-94). In 11:56-58 the bowl enters Manimekalai's hand at that pool on that day (கோமுகி வலம் செய்து ... பாத்திரம் புகுதலும்). This is a condition and its fulfilment, so the teaches point, that her receiving it is a verdict on her compassion, follows from the Tamil.

243 makes the gift of wives a charge (தன்னை ஈந்ததும் தாரங்கள் ஈந்ததும் ... அறம் கொண்டவன்). In 398.4 the narrator tags the Buddhist speaker with the same figure: பெண்டானம் ஈயும் அறங்கொண்ட பெருமையினான். The shared figure carries a sneer from argument into narration. 'Standing epithet' slightly overstates a single occurrence.

Mokkalan's dilemma in 381 is about qualities and the thing that bears them (குணங்களல் லாற்பொருள் வேறில்லை ... ஒன்றெனின் ... ஒன்றுரை), and it is a debating move put up to be answered. The Manimekalai's ஒற்றுமை நயம் and வேற்றுமை நயம் concern cause and effect (காரண காரியம் ஆகிய பொருள்களை ஒன்றா உணர்தல்). The tension joins different topics, and the claim that the Buddhist nayas come 'close to the Jain answer' is not in either text.

The blessing does keep the patikam's ஊழ்வினை moral (தொல்லை வினையால் துயருழந்தாள்) and praises the king who gave his life (உயிர் கொடுத்த கோவேந்தன் வாழியரோ), which turns அரைசியல் பிழைத்தோர்க்கு அறம்கூற்று ஆவது from warning to praise. But the note says the blessing hails 'the king dharma killed', while the Tamil says her tears killed him (கண்ணின்நீர் கொல்ல). The note is inaccurate on that point.

The two halves of one story are joined. 6:20-24 tells the curse (நாடகம் உருப்பசி நல்காளாகி ... மண்மிசைத் தங்குக இவள் எனச் சாபம் பெற்ற மங்கை மாதவி), and 3:1-3 tells heavenly women freed from a sage's curse at the தலைக்கோல் தானம். But in kaathai 3 the curse ends at the talaikkol place for the heavenly women, and nothing says Madhavi's own first performance ended it. The teaches' 'a curse that her first performance was said to end' misstates the third kaathai, and 3:6 (பிறப்பிற் குன்றா) does not settle descent.
links.text_issue: The syntax of 6:20-24 (who is cursed, Urvasi or a second dancer) is not settled; the marker flagged both units as uncertain.

links.reason: The reversal is real. கோலின் செம்மை and தீதுதீர் மதுரை (15:3, 9) stand against தளர்ந்தசெங் கோலன் and யானே கள்வன் (20:83-85). But the sceptre praise of lines 1-6 is the narrator's description of the city Kovalan sees, not his own words, and the teaches overreaches: the king condemns himself on the evidence of the gem (மணி கண்டு), not by Kovalan's measure, and 'the day before his death' is not in the text.

Both texts concern the gift of one's own flesh, and Puram 43 praises the dove-saving ancestor's வரையா ஈகை. But Neelakesi's test is that no living person asks for flesh, eyes or heads (வாழு மாந்தர் உழைவருவாரில்லை), and in the Sibi story a hawk does ask, so the objection does not squarely meet the poem. 'Tamil tradition did not hold it as a settled virtue' generalises from one polemic aimed at Buddhist jataka gifts, and the Purananuru side gains only a generic 'met a challenge'.

97 names two sins separately (கொன்ற பாவம் ... ஊன் தின்ற பாவம்), so eating flesh is a fault even for one who did not kill. 163 opens the charge against the Buddha with ஊன்றின்றல் இழுக்கென்னான். The sermon gives the doctrinal ground for the first charge, and the note says so.

Kural 388 says the ruler who does justice and protects is held as இறை by the people. Senguttuvan says birth into a line that guards the people is துன்பம் அல்லது தொழுதக வில், speaking of the burden as the king feels it (மழைவளங் கரப்பின் வான்பேர் அச்சம்). The two speak from different standpoints, the subjects' honour and the ruler's experience, so the pair limits the couplet rather than contradicting it, and 'judge the same office oppositely' overstates the conflict.

Naladiyar 195 says நல்ல குலம், தீய குலம் are only words, and that lineage comes from தவம் கல்வி ஆள்வினை. Aputtiran answers the brahmins from inside their own tradition with seers born of cow, deer, tiger and jackal (ஆன் மகன் அசலன் ... நரி மகன் ... கேசகம்பளன்) and asks ஆவொடு வந்த அழி குலம் உண்டோ. The pairing shows the same denial of birth rank made once as a principle and once as a charge of inconsistency, and both gains clauses hold.

The descriptions are accurate: 27:57-77 lists eight பிரமாண ஆபாசங்கள் (திரியக் கோடல், ஐயம் ...), and 29:450-472 closes the அனுமான ஆபாசம் rules. But neither unit limits the other. The teaches contrast, cognition against argument, compares the logician's whole list with only the final, inference-only section of Aravanar's lesson, so it does not show that the two schools divide the ground differently.
links.text_issue: Line 29:463 (என்றால் என்று நின்ற இடத்து) reads awkwardly and may be corrupt.

links.reason: The vow (பத்தினியே யாமாகில் ஒட்டேன் அரசோடு ஒழிப்பேன் மதுரையும், 21:36-37) is followed by the housewives' verdict கொங்கைப் பூசல் கொடிதோ அன்று (22:136), which is a real answer to it. But the teaches says the vow is answered 'not by a god'. In fact the fire god appears and burns the city at her bidding (21:49-56), so the main answer to the vow is divine, and the wives only approve of it.

The materialist dismisses knowledge of a former birth as the product of தெய்வ மயக்கு or dreams (27:281-283). In Silap. 30 the former births return after a god appears on the brahmin woman (மறையோள் தன்மேல் தோன்றி) and the water is sprinkled (ஒளித்த பிறப்புவந் துற்றது), before the court. The claims are incompatible on the same means of knowledge, and the teaches rightly treats the Manimekalai's line as a sceptic's view rather than the sister epic's own.

874 argues that a newborn's going to the breast cannot be the work of the five elements newly joined (ஐந்து பூதமும் செறிந்த நாள்களுள் செய்வன வல்ல). That is evidence a materialist cannot wave away as தெய்வ மயக்கு or dream, which is a fair point. But 874 is about the knower, not memory of former birth, and it does not limit the Manimekalai passage. It supplies a stronger argument against the same opponent, which is better called develops.

The image is shared. The fleeing kings become ஆடு கூத்தர் (26:228) in disguise, and Maadalan likens the soul to ஆடுங் கூத்தர் that does not stay in one கோலம் (28:165-166). But Maadalan's point is the king's own ageing and the soul's passage by deeds. The teaches' claim that the kings' disguise was 'mocked by the king's rivals' and that 'the mockery recoils on the mocker' is not in either unit.

445.2 defines the Lord's greatness by அட்டக வித்து வெந்தாம், the eightfold seeds burnt. 458 takes up the burnt seed (வித்தென்றும் வெந்தால் முளையலது) to answer whether release is extinction: the soul abides நித்தியமாகி in சித்தி. One image is extended from definition to the answer of an objection, and the note says which.
links.text_issue: 445 lines 3-4 are loose in syntax; the link rests on line 2, which is clear.

links.reason: Both are elephant-taming feats: Kovalan's கடக்களிறு அடக்கிய கருணை மறவ (15:52-53) and Udayakumaran's கடுங்கண் யானையின் கடாத் திறம் அடக்கி (4:46). The image is shared. But Udayakumaran is not chasing Manimekalai when he quells the beast, which is his own runaway mount in the city. The contrast 'compassion once and desire the second time' reads a motive into the Manimekalai scene that the Tamil does not give.

Neelakesi cites the chain உண்டியால் உடம்பு, உடம்பினால் உணர்வு as common knowledge. Tirumular argues from the body to knowledge (உடம்பார் அழியில் ... மெய்ஞ்ஞானஞ் சேரவு மாட்டார்) but says nothing of food. So the 'same chain, food to body to knowledge' is only half shared. The other side's gain, that the premise 'licenses only bare food', rests on Neelakesi's last line, which is uncertain (பண்டியாற் போக்கு).
links.text_issue: Neelakesi 282 line 4 (பண்டியாற் போக்குநின்பஃறொடர்ப்பாடு) is uncertain in sense and carries a repaired ஃ.

links.reason: In the Silappathikaram Kannaki declares கோநகர் சீறினேன் குற்றமிலேன் யான், and the fire burns at her bidding (பொற்றொடி ஏவ). In the Manimekalai the same Kannaki says சீற்றம் கொண்டு செழு நகர் சிதைத்தேன் after hearing the truth, and names the act அடு சினப் பாவம், whose fruit will reach her (எய்துதல் ஒழியாது). The two make incompatible judgements on one act, and the teaches names the point on which they turn.

Both name the burning of Kama: Neelakesi's வெல்லற் கரிய அனங்கனை வெண்ணீறாக வெகுண்டோய் against Pattinathar's காமனைக் கண்ணால் எரிக்கக் கனல்விழித்த காரணன். The image is truly shared. But 'the victory over desire that the Saiva texts reserve for the Lord' is not something Siddhar 603 claims. Nor does the Jain hymn's point limit the Siddhar line, so this is a shared image, and the claim of a contest overstates both gains.

In Puhar the warriors offer their own heads so that the king's trouble be removed and his strength have a bulwark (மன்னற்கு உற்றதை ஒழிக்க ... வலிக்குவரம்பு ஆக). In the same city Champapathi answers that lives were given for kings, yet the burning ground holds a thousand kings' shrines (உலக மன்னவர்க்கு உயிர்க்கு உயிர் ஈவோர் இலரோ ... ஆயிரம் கோட்டம்). The note hedges on the reading the conflict depends on, as the brief asks.

The epic names only திருமா வளவன, and Puram 66 is addressed to கரிகால் வளவ. Nothing in these lines fixes that they are one king, and the marker himself notes that the Tamil supports only a shared name. The teaches about 'the later memory of the Chola' losing the Sangam check depends entirely on that identification.

The deed is the same: குருகொடு பெயர் பெற்ற மால் வரை உடைத்து (Pari 5.9) against நெட்டைக் க்ரவுஞ்சம் பிளந்து (Tp 38). The observation that the Sangam poet gives the hill by its crane meaning while Arunagirinathar borrows the Sanskrit name is true. But the later hymn does not extend the earlier one; this is a shared mythic image with a naming difference.
links.text_issue: Paripadal 5 lines 12-14 are not in the comparison edition, and line 5 carries a restored vowel sign.

links.reason: Kural 911 speaks of women who seek wealth and not love (அன்பின் விழையார் பொருள்விழையும்). Madhavi's letter after the wealth is gone shows her outside that class, and Kovalan clears her (தன்றீ திலள், என்தீது). That is a case the couplet's condition already excludes, not one the rule 'cannot explain', so the pair marks the rule's limit rather than contradicting it.

158.2 praises a Lord who never says 'I will speak' yet has a drum-like voice (கூறுவேனெனக் கூறாய் குரன்முரசனையதோர் குணத்தை). That is the Jain answer to the Ajivika charge Neelakesi takes up in 682, that a knower who speaks falls into ஆர்வம் and சினம். The link is real. But 682 itself answers by reductio (the silent man would be a சிற்றாத்தன்), not by the hymn's paradox, and 'aimed at this debate' says more than a hymn sung long before can show.
links.text_issue: 682 line 4 is compressed and its turn is the marker's reading.

links.reason: Both commend food. கொடுப்பின் அசனங் கொடுக்க and அற்றார் அழிபசி தீர்த்தல் ... பொருள்வைப்புழி. But the Nanmanikkadigai names no recipient and the Kural no gift, and the teaches only adds the two claims together. It is the shared theme, with no development.

The verses share the phrase உடம்பொடு உயிரிடை (Neelakesi 64.1, Kural 338.2), which the note does not mention. Neelakesi's sage knows the way that cuts the deeds bound up in the body-soul ஒற்றுமை வேற்றுமை, while the Kural's point is that the tie simply ends. The contrast holds, but the Neelakesi clause is an epithet in a verse whose action is the sage seeing through a deceiver. The epic-side gain, being 'placed against a commonplace', names nothing specific.
links.text_issue: Neelakesi 64 is printed with the number 6, and line 3 is obscure.

links.reason: The teaches says Kannaki 'keeps the burning of Madurai as her own act', but the unit says only that she lost her husband when வல்வினை வந்து உருத்தகாலை and that Madurai and its kingship came to ruin. கடுவினையேன் is most naturally the common self-description 'I of harsh fate', not a claim of agency. The 'fate and agent together' reading stretches one word.

Kavunthi's saying (வானம் பொய்யாது ... வேந்தர் கொற்றம் சிதையாது பத்தினிப் பெண்டிர் இருந்த நாடு) does extend the chaste wife's power from rain to the king's victory, a real qualification. But the teaches says the couplet 'keeps the wife below the gods', when தெய்வம் தொழாஅள் sets her apart from god-worship, not beneath the gods. The epic-side gain claims the Kural as the saying's 'source', which the text, calling it அத்தகு நல்லுரை, does not establish.

Both refuse praised beauty on the evidence of the burning ground, and the words overlap: பல்லென்பும் ... புறங்காட்டுள் against புறங்காட்டு உதிர்ந்துக்க பல்லென்பு. The quatrain's speaker has seen it (கண்டு ஒழுகுவேன), while the sage dwells there (உறைவன்), so the memory-against-way-of-life contrast is in the Tamil. Both gains hold, since the sage's temptress is a real test of the quatrain's resolve.

203 puts the dilemma to Kundalakesi: a சத்தி that passes on is a sixth beside the five (பொருளோடு ஆறு ஆகாவோ), and without it there is முழுக்கேடு. 580 puts the same shape to the Buddha: the lac is வேறொன்று beside the seed, but nothing beyond the five aggregates is shown (ஐந்திற்கும் வேறொன்று காட்டாய்). The same argument against two opponents shows that the case is one argument.

The kings' 'எமது ஈது' and the sage's 'இருஞ் செரு ஒழிமின் எமது ஈது' are the same words, and their பெரும் பற்று (57) is set against the sage's claim, so reading the scene through பற்றுக பற்றற்றான் பற்றினை is a real addition to it. But the Tamil does not show the kings taking up the sage's clinging; it says only that the seat appeared where the sage had preached. The other-side gain, 'the moment the substituted clinging takes hold', is not in the text.

Kundalakesi 19 has a steadfast man who can say பாரித்தது எல்லாம் வினையின் பயன், which is the tenet Neelakesi attributes to her opponents (நுமர் ... எப்பொழுதும் உரைப்ப) and turns against the Buddha's suffering for others. The two do not conflict; the fragment states the tenet that Neelakesi uses. So the pair is better called develops, and the fragment names no Buddha.
links.text_issue: Kundalakesi 19 is a fragment with an unnamed subject; the marker flagged its sense as uncertain.

links.reason: The doctrinal conflict over the momentary mind is real. The Manimekalai lists சித்தம் உற்பவித்தது மின்போல் among the வழக்கு modes, and Neelakesi asks how perishing is known if the mind perishes with what it knew (உணர்ந்தவற்றோடு அறக்கெட்டு ... இறப்பறிதல் எவனாகும்). But 196 does not take up the lightning image or the speech modes. The teaches' claim that one side offers 'a manner of speaking' rests on the marker's uncertain assignment of examples at 208-213.
links.text_issue: The marker flagged the assignment of examples at Manimekalai 30:208-213 as uncertain.

links.reason: The phrase is shared: கடவுட் பத்தினிக் கற்கால் கொண்டபின் (27:2) against கடவுள் பத்தினிக் கற்கோள் வேண்டி (patikam 4), with the Ganga in both (கங்கைப் பேர்யாற்று; கங்கை மண்ணி). Senguttuvan is named in both, so this is a sound connection. But the teaches and the epic-side gain treat the preface as a prior and independent 'Chera tradition' on which the epic 'rests'. Nothing in the Tamil sets the direction: the preface may draw on the epic's story, so 'outside witness' is not established.

The formula recurs almost word for word: பதினோர் ஆடலும் பாட்டின் பகுதியும் விதிமாண் கொள்கையின் விளங்க (6:66-67) against பதினோர் ஆடலும் பாட்டும் கொட்டும் விதிமாண் கொள்கையின் விளங்க (3:14-15). But in kaathai 3 the formula describes the dance master's knowledge (3:12-25), not Madhavi's training (3:1-11), and the teaches adds little beyond the repetition itself.

313 argues that the sin of killing reaches the eater even without intention (சென்று சேர்தலைச் சித்தம் இன்மையால் is the rejected Buddhist rule). 595 argues the other direction: where mind is there is action (சித்தமுண்டவ்வழிச் செய்கையும் உண்டே). The theses are related but not the same, and the claim that 313's quarrel 'rests on' 595's thesis does not follow, since one says sin without intent and the other says intent implies act.

760 says that for those who have made bright wealth, ஏனை இரண்டும் ஒருங்கு, the other two aims, are easy. 39 says only what comes through aram is pleasure. The two are compatible: wealth can make virtue easy, and pleasure can still come only through virtue. The teaches ('the order differs by book') names no conflict.

59 has Neelakesi appear in Kamalekai's form (காமலேகை தன் உருவொடு), and 134 has her drop the illusory form (மாய உருவம் மாறித் தன் மற்றை உருவமே கொண்டு) and confess as பேயேன். The reversal is real, but it is largely the story's own sequence. The teaches, that conversion starts with confession before doctrine, is true but thin.
